description:
Record a NEW decision or instruction of the master that will be passed to ALL implementor agents and the verifier. Use for:
        |1) DECISIONS ON PLAYER REQUESTS: if the player asks for something non-standard (a non-standard class combination, a custom ability, an action against the rules) — be sure to record your decision here, do not leave the interpretation to the implementors.
        |2) ATMOSPHERIC/CONCEPTUAL INSTRUCTIONS: the general concept of the character, the setting, key context.
        |If a decision with that textId already exists — use updateDecision (this tool will return an error).
        |The master's decisions take priority over D&D rules and any wishes of the player. The implementors and the verifier must follow them.
name: addDecision

decision.description: Brief and unambiguous decision, for example 'DENIED — spell above the class level', 'APPROVED — a druid with a longbow', 'Setting: Slavic fantasy'.

reason.description: The decision's IDEA — WHY it exists, what concept/rules problem it solves — the essence in ONE phrase.

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments. If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description: Add a task for the implementor of one of the character-pipeline domains (BASE/BIO/STATS/FEATURES/SPELLS/PROFICIENCIES/EQUIPMENT). Use a separate call for each task. The name differs from `addTask` because `addTask` is reserved by the framework for fix-tasks the planner assigns itself in SELF_REVIEW.
name: addImplementorTask

domain.description: Domain (part of the character): BASE, BIO, STATS, FEATURES, SPELLS, PROFICIENCIES, EQUIPMENT

type.description: Operation type: CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, FIX

description.description: Task description for the implementor agent

criticality.description: Task criticality: LOW, NORMAL, HIGH, CRITICAL

reason.description: The task's IDEA — WHY the result is needed by the character/concept, the essence in ONE phrase. Not a retelling of the description in other words! For FIX the reason for the fix is acceptable.

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments. If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description: Write a note to the player. **Default — do NOT call, in both phases (INITIAL and REVIEW).** This is NOT a report on the work done. THE KEY DISTINCTION (the model confuses exactly this): filling in what the player did NOT specify (race/class/name/background/spells/gear for a general, brief or random request) is the master's normal work, it does NOT require a note, stay silent. Use ONLY on one of three occasions: WARNING (the player asked for a SPECIFIC thing and you gave something that is NOT it — a refusal/trimming/substituting an analogue; without an explicit unfulfilled request — do NOT write), QUESTION (without a clarification from the player the sheet physically cannot be assembled — a last resort), INFO (ONLY if playerRequest contains a VERBATIM question — a "?" sign or "why/how/is it possible/what if"; no question → INFO is FORBIDDEN). It is FORBIDDEN to write a report "assembled the character", "created a warrior for you", "here is your hero", "changed the class", "chose the spells", "took the request into account, assembled Y", "did everything per the request" — neither as INFO nor as WARNING; the result is already visible in the character sheet, such a note only clutters the feed and spends tokens. The notes fully replace the previous player.notes snapshot — no call = empty feedback, for a typical creation by description this is the CORRECT result. Open QUESTIONs from previousPlayerNotes: if the player answered in playerRequest — INFO "took the clarification about X into account"; if the question is still relevant — rewrite it with the same QUESTION anew. The player's language, a conversational style, not a technical log.
name: addPlayerNote

type.description: Note type. WARNING — the player asked for a SPECIFIC thing and you gave something else (a refusal/trimming/substituting an analogue); filling in the unspecified is NOT a WARNING. QUESTION — A LAST RESORT: every question = a whole extra generation cycle, only if the sheet physically cannot be assembled without the answer; in doubt — choose WARNING. INFO — ONLY an answer to the player's VERBATIM question (the "?" sign) from playerRequest; no question → INFO is forbidden; it is NOT a "what I did" report.

text.description: Note text in the player's language (Russian, if the game is in Russian).

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments. If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description: Record a new task for yourself as a result of self-review. Available ONLY in the SELF_REVIEW phase. After adding all tasks call transitionTo into the working phase — the frame will execute them there.
name: addTask

description.description: What exactly needs to be done

description: FULL RESET: Reset all the existing character's data, INCLUDING the accumulated appearance history (`appearances`). After `clearAll` the old portraits/tokens are not inherited — the new character will have a fresh 'base' appearance generated from scratch. Use ONLY when a `player-request` finding requires REPLACING the character with another (a different race/class, 'generate another', 'a random new one'). Never call on technical errors from the verifier and never if the character does not exist yet.
name: clearAll

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments. If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description: Mark the task as done. Use this tool after you have performed all the actions described in the task or fixed the problem found by the setter.
name: completeTask

reason.description: Optional: closing reason/comment. Required for "decision items" of the checklist (for example, refusing a book promotion): such an item is closed by a SEPARATE call with an explicit reason, not silently in a common batch.

description: Mark several tasks as done in one call. Use for going through the working phase's checklist in a row (for example, closing several 'chk-*' items) when there are no intermediate decisions between them. If an idea appears along the way — close them one by one via completeTask. REVIEW items ('rev-*', the self-check phase) are NOT closed by this tool: each requires a separate completeTask with a verdict-specific in reason, batch closing is rejected.
name: completeTasks

ids.description: List of task IDs to close

description: Request regeneration of the character's portrait+token. AN EXPENSIVE OPERATION (~\$0.10, 1-2 minutes). Call ONLY on a cardinal change of look: a change of race/sex/age, a transformation (wild-shape/polymorph/into a beast/into undead), a return of form, a permanent magical transformation, the appearance/removal of scars/tattoos, a cardinal change of hairstyle. A change of armor, weapon, shield, any gear and cosmetic changes are NOT a reason (the portrait is conditionally abstract). For a new character (CREATE from scratch with no existing character) the portrait is generated automatically — this call is not needed.
name: requestImageRegeneration

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments. If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description: Transition to another state (phase) of work. Call it once the current phase's work is complete — as the LAST call of the SAME response that finishes that work (when the phase rules allow the transition). The switch is applied at the END of this response: every other call in the same response still runs in the CURRENT phase, so it is safe to finish the phase's work and request the transition together. Do not spend a separate response on a lone transition call, and do not place new work AFTER the transition expecting the new phase.
name: transitionTo

description: Update a previously recorded master's decision (by exact textId). Use to bring canonical wordings up to date: for example, a new interpretation of the same disputed question appeared. Do not breed duplicates via addDecision — for an existing textId always use updateDecision.
name: updateDecision

textId.description: textId of an existing decision. If there is no decision with that textId — an error; use addDecision.

decision.description: New decision text (fully replaces the old one).

reason.description: New decision IDEA — WHY it exists, in one phrase (fully replaces the old one).

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments. If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description: Update an already assigned implementor task by its id — reword the description (or change the criticality/reason) WITHOUT recreating the whole plan. The domain and task type do not change (to change them, delete the task and create a new one). If there is no task with that id — an error. Use instead of clearAll when a couple of tasks need pinpoint fixing.
name: updateImplementorTask

description.description: New task description (fully replaces the old one).

criticality.description: New criticality (optional — omit to keep the current one).

reason.description: New task IDEA (optional — omit to keep the current one).

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments. If the call returns an error, the wrapper itself will NOT close the task. Don't use it for partial progress; for multi-tool tasks, close via completeTask after the final step.

description: 🦴 Start building a character from a READY SKELETON from the library (the "SKELETONS FROM THE LIBRARY" block in the context) instead of an empty sheet. The service will copy the SKELETON mechanics (classes/levels/stats/features/spells/proficiencies/attacks/gear) as the starting state, while the IDENTITY (name/appearance/backstory/personality) and the LOOK (portrait/token) are always assembled ANEW for the player's request — the skeleton is depersonalized. Call on INITIAL, BEFORE assigning tasks, ONLY if the shown skeleton is really close to the concept (the same class/level/archetype combination; name/race do not matter — you will override them). If none fits — do not call, build from scratch. skeletonId — the display HANDLE (`lib:…`) strictly from the shown block.
name: useSkeleton

skeletonId.description: HANDLE for showing the skeleton (`lib:…`, exactly as in the card of the "SKELETONS FROM THE LIBRARY" block).

closesTaskId.description: Optional. ID of the task or issue that is FULLY resolved by THIS call — pass it OPTIMISTICALLY when you are confident in the arguments.
